candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: incorporate client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care; use therapeutic communication and support psychosocial needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural beliefs/practices and individualized care
candidate.educational_objective: Provide culturally responsive care by eliciting the individual client's beliefs, practices, and preferences rather than stereotyping, and integrate relevant preferences into safe care planning.

options.A: Use a standardized cultural profile to predict preferences instead of asking the individual client about values or practices.
options.B: Exclude cultural practices from the plan whenever biomedical treatment is available, even when the practices are safe.
options.C: Avoid discussing culture or health beliefs so cultural differences cannot influence communication or care planning.
options.D: Ask about the individual client’s cultural values, health beliefs, and preferences and incorporate relevant practices when compatible with safe, effective care.

candidate.rationale: HHS National CLAS Standard 1 calls for effective, understandable, respectful care and services responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy, and communication needs. HHS also describes CLAS as respecting the whole individual and responding to the individual's health needs and preferences. D is therefore the culturally responsive approach.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Culturally responsive care should be respectful of and responsive to the individual client's cultural health beliefs, practices, communication needs and preferences rather than relying on stereotypes.
candidate.source_document_title: National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care
candidate.source_locator: Principal Standard 1: provide effective, understandable and respectful quality care/services responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy and communication needs. What is CLAS?: respect the whole individual and respond to the individual's health needs and preferences.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health
candidate.source_version_date: Current National CLAS Standards; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A nurse plans care for a client whose cultural background differs from the nurse’s. Which action best reflects culturally responsive nursing care?
